mcat_description.short: Prefabricated and pre-engineered steel buildings designed for agricultural use, including poultry sheds, dairy units, grain storage structures, cattle barns, farm equipment sheds, and workers' accommodation — supplied as factory-fabricated component kits assembled on-site.
mcat_description.long: Agricultural buildings in the Indian B2B market are predominantly Pre-Engineered Buildings (PEB) and prefabricated steel structures purpose-built for farm and agribusiness infrastructure needs. Components — including primary steel frames, roof purlins, wall girts, roofing sheets, and insulated sandwich panels — are manufactured in a factory to custom design specifications and shipped to the farm site for rapid on-site assembly. Common types include poultry sheds, dairy cattle shelters, grain and hay storage godowns, tractor and farm equipment parking sheds, and farm workers' accommodation blocks. Structural design follows IS 800:2007 (steel structures) and IS 875 (loads on buildings), with the National Building Code of India 2016 providing overarching compliance guidance for prefabricated construction.

market_context: Agricultural buildings in India are a sub-segment of the broader Pre-Engineered Buildings (PEB) and prefabricated structures market. Multiple market research sources confirm agricultural buildings hold approximately 10% of the Indian PEB market by application, with the segment driven by growing emphasis on sustainable farming and efficient storage infrastructure. Steel is the dominant material for prefabricated agricultural structures in India, valued for strength, durability, recyclability, and faster construction versus brick-and-mortar. Leading Indian manufacturers active in this segment include EPACK Prefab, Pressmach, and iBeeHive Steel Structures. Structural compliance in India follows IS 800:2007 for steel design, IS 875 for load calculations (wind, live, dead loads), IS 15917:2010 for mixed/composite prefabricated construction, and the National Building Code of India 2016 as the overarching framework. Buyers evaluate structures on span width, bay length, roof pitch, ventilation design, roofing sheet type (colour-coated/galvanised), insulation (sandwich panel vs bare sheet), and wind/seismic zone compliance. The Indian prefabricated buildings market overall was valued at approximately USD 15 billion in 2024–2025 and is projected to grow at ~8.8–8.95% CAGR through 2030, with agricultural applications as a smaller but growing sub-segment (single source for 10% share figure — low confidence on exact share).
